name: Congenital Hereditary Endothelial Dystrophy

criteria.description: Presence of bilateral diffuse corneal clouding from birth or early infancy
Histopathologic or specular microscopy evidence of endothelial cell abnormalities and thickened Descemet membrane
Positive family history consistent with autosomal recessive or dominant inheritance
No signs of corneal inflammation or scarring

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Bilateral corneal clouding from birth or early infancy plus endothelial cell abnormalities on microscopy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing for SLC4A11 mutations can support diagnosis

pathognomonic.notes: Typically present at birth or early infancy

pathognomonic.symptomName: Corneal edema due to endothelial dysfunction

laboratory: Specular microscopy showing decreased endothelial cell density and abnormal morphology
Histopathology revealing thickened Descemet membrane with abnormal endothelial cells
imaging: Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) demonstrating increased corneal thickness
genetic: Rare mutations in ZEB1 and other genes reported
other: Slit-lamp examination revealing diffuse corneal haze without vascularization

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of central corneal opacity with iridocorneal adhesions
Often associated with anterior segment dysgenesis

redFlags: Rapidly progressive corneal clouding with vision loss
Corneal scarring or neovascularization indicating possible infection or inflammation
references: Weiss JS, Møller HU, Lisch W, et al. The IC3D classification of corneal dystrophies–edition 2. Cornea. 2015;34(2):117-159.
Vithana EN, Morgan PE, Ramprasad V, et al. SLC4A11 mutations in congenital hereditary endothelial dystrophy. Am J Hum Genet. 2006;79(2):354-359.
Møller HU. Congenital hereditary endothelial dystrophy. Dev Ophthalmol. 2011;48:59-66.
